Every rebrand has a root cause. If one of these sounds like your business, this process was built to fix it. Pick a trigger to filter them.

1External
Corporate change

New leadership, ownership transfer, or company pivot forces a brand reset to reflect the new direction and remove legacy associations.

2External
Competition

A competitor rebranded or entered the space: staying put means being confused with them or losing perceived differentiation in the market.

3External
Mergers and de-mergers

Two companies combining, or one splitting off, creates identity conflict. A unified or separated brand removes confusion and builds trust with both audiences.

4Strategic
Structural realignment

Spin-offs, department splits, or portfolio restructuring require each entity to have a distinct, standalone brand identity.

5Strategic
Market insight and gaps

Research revealed an underserved niche or positioning gap. The rebrand repositions the business to own that space before a competitor does.

6Strategic
Product life cycle

The company expanded into new products or services that the current brand doesn't cover: a refresh or brand architecture update is needed to contain it all.

7Strategic
Intellectual property

The business needs to trademark, license, or franchise: the brand must be distinctive enough legally and visually to protect and scale.

8Strategic
Corporate strategy

New 3 to 5 year goals, investor commitments, or market expansion plans require the brand to communicate ambition and credibility at a higher level.

9Brand equity
Change of perception

The current brand is associated with low quality, old pricing, or a wrong audience. A rebrand signals the business has fundamentally changed.

10Brand equity
Relevance and authenticity

The brand feels dated or inauthentic to today's audience. Founders want the visual and verbal identity to match who they've actually become.

11Brand equity
The need to simplify

Messaging is confusing, the logo is cluttered, or the offer is hard to explain. A rebrand strips it back to one clear, ownable idea that sells itself.

12Performance
Performance

Sales are declining, leads are poor quality, or conversion is low. The brand is failing to attract or close the right clients and needs a strategic reset.

The method

The Productized Expertise System

Five steps that turn your real method into a productized expert business, from a recorded deep-dive to a live launch.

1

Extract

A recorded deep-dive interview mines your real method, the actions, decisions, and mistakes that drive results, not the theory.

2

Structure

We compress it into a named 3 to 7 phase signature framework, each module tied to one clear outcome.

3

Script

Every lesson written to one fixed beat, hook, teach, example, pitfall, recap. Under 8 minutes each.

4

Produce

Batch recorded with the right format per lesson, human, screen-share, or AI avatar. Captioned and thumbnailed.

5

Launch

A discounted beta pre-sale tests demand before the full build, then modules drip while the first cohort runs.

Built for

One system, shaped to your field

The same method adapts to the way each expert sells. Here is what it becomes across six fields.

⚖️

Lawyer

Your repeatable legal process as a named system, for example The Contract Defence Method, sold as modules, templates, and contract walkthroughs.

🎨

Designer

Your eye as a teachable framework, teardown videos, swipe files, and critique modules, then a paid cohort.

FAQ

Questions before every project

The things founders always ask before they start. Answered directly, no fluff.

🛡️How does the money-back guarantee actually work?
If we miss the agreed delivery deadline, or the final delivery is materially incomplete versus the agreed scope, you get a full refund. No negotiation, no credit note. The only exceptions are delays caused by the client: late questionnaire submission or scope changes after commencement.
💡Why is there a RM290 entry offer? Is the quality lower?
No. The entry offer exists to remove the risk of the first transaction. The RM290 logo mark uses the same methodology and team as a RM30,000 architecture project. The difference is scope, not quality. Most clients who start at RM290 move to a larger engagement within 60 days.
⏱️How long does a typical project take?
Entry offers deliver in 7 days. Websites deliver in 1 to 3 weeks depending on tier, and a scoped app build ships in about 3 weeks, our AI-accelerated workflow means projects now move in weeks, not months. Larger custom builds and full brand architecture have timelines agreed at kickoff. The clock starts from questionnaire submission, not from payment.
🗺️Do you work with clients outside Kuala Lumpur?
Yes. The majority of our process is fully remote by design. Kickoff, reviews, and delivery happen via WhatsApp, email, and video call. We have active clients across Peninsular Malaysia, East Malaysia, and Singapore. In-person sessions are available for Klang Valley clients on request.
💳What payment methods do you accept?
We accept bank transfer, ToyyibPay, and DuitNow QR. For projects above RM5,000 we offer a 50/30/20 split: 50% to start, 30% at the halfway milestone, 20% on final delivery. Full upfront is not required for larger projects.
⚙️What is Methodas and do I need it?
Methodas is our systems and education platform for founders who want to build without hiring an agency full-time. It gives you access to the same frameworks we use for clients. If you want it done for you, BrandMethod is for you. If you want to learn and build yourself, Methodas is for you. Many clients use both.
🔄How many revisions do I get?
Every project includes a defined number of revision rounds in the scope. Entry offers include one round. Growth and premium tiers include two to three. Revisions are based on the original brief. Direction changes after commencement are treated as scope changes and priced separately.
🏆How is BrandMethod different from Fiverr?
Fiverr delivers an asset. BrandMethod delivers a system. You get a dedicated PM, a written guarantee, a defined timeline, a growth pathway, and a Malaysian team that understands the local market and SME landscape specifically. The strategy behind the asset is what separates them.
📂Who owns the final files and the rights once it’s done?
You do, fully. On final payment you own every deliverable outright, including the editable master and source files. No licensing, no subscriptions, and no being locked into us to keep using your own brand. Any designer or developer can pick the files up later.
🧭What do you need from me to get started?
A completed onboarding brief, and for larger projects a short kickoff or strategy session. The brief takes anywhere from a few minutes to about an hour depending on the package, and the more honest and complete it is, the sharper the result. After that the work is largely on us, with clear checkpoints for your feedback.
🧾Will there be any hidden or extra costs?
No surprises. Every package is fixed-price and quoted before you pay. The only separate costs are genuine third-party pass-throughs: government trademark fees, your ad spend, hosting, and those are billed at cost with no markup, and flagged upfront.
⬆️Can I start with a smaller package and upgrade later?
Yes, and we build it so you’re never penalised for starting small. Lower tiers credit toward higher ones: audit fees come off the build that follows, and website upgrade credit carries part of what you’ve already paid into the bigger version. Start where you are and scale when it makes sense.
📊Do I have to pay the full amount upfront?
For entry offers, yes, they’re a single payment, which keeps them fast and low-risk. Larger projects run on 50/30/20 milestone payments: to begin, at the midpoint, and on final delivery, so what you pay tracks the progress of the work.
